statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail remains at the upper watch band because the reported strike on an Iranian tanker near Kharg Island adds a credible Gulf reopening-gap amplifier, while weekend closure prevents live confirmation of persistent Nasdaq structure.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: WATCH; Tail remains below the block threshold. Stress is extreme because Gulf, oil, and rate risks are elevated, but no live Nasdaq continuation or failed-retracement path is available during the weekend closure.
headline: Kharg tanker strike keeps weekend Tail at WATCH while NQ remains closed
body: Reuters reports that an Iranian tanker near Kharg Island was hit and that Tasnim attributed the strike to U.S. missiles, while U.S. confirmation was not immediately available. The event raises reopening-gap sensitivity, but the closed NQ market provides no live evidence of persistent mean-reversion failure.

lookbackSummary: The prior 24 hours covered Friday's post-payroll repricing, two brief orange Tail episodes during live trading, the transition into weekend closure, and a later return to WATCH after the Kharg tanker-strike report. Once live price discovery ended, Tail otherwise stayed low because no persistent Nasdaq path could be observed.
outlookSummary: NQ remains closed throughout this 24-hour horizon. If no additional verified Gulf escalation or material Hormuz disruption appears, Tail is projected to ease gradually within WATCH as the Kharg headline ages; Stress stays extreme from conflict, oil, and rate pressure, while confidence declines as Friday's live evidence becomes older.
